Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can note that I was the driver of the vehicle involved.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where the collision happened?
A: It was on a surface street in Katy, Texas, near a shopping center. I was heading toward the intersection when the
other car came over into my lane.
Q: What was your speed at the time?
A: I'd say I was going maybe twenty-five miles an hour. Traffic was light and I had just started to slow down.
Q: Did you brake or swerve before impact?
A: I braked hard and tired to steer right, but there wasn't much room. It was more of a glancing hit than a full crash,
although the airbags did not deploy.
Q: Did you hit your head or lose consciousness?
A: No, I didn't hit my head and I stayed awake the whole time. I just felt a jolt through my body.
Q: Have you had any pain since the collision?
A: Yes, my lower back has been sore since then. It's a tight, aching feeling, worse when I sit for a long time or get up
from a chair. A doctor told me it looks like a back strain.
Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment?
A: I went to urgent care the same day and I've been doing physical therapy twice a week. I'm also taking an
over-the-counter anti-inflammatory when the pain flares up.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I want to get back to normal as soon as I can. I'm willing to prvoide my medical records if you need them.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
</page>
